answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that deposit when independently checkable evidence shows coordinated abuse. This does not make identities impossible to forge; it makes a Sybil swarm costly, because every additional account needs capital that remains exposed for the dispute horizon. A rising tide of fake accounts therefore raises the attacker’s locked funds and potential losses, while honest agents can challenge suspicious clusters.
